title: Parser: a deeply nested statement is refused as too complex
verdict: `FAILED_TO_PARSE_TOO_COMPLEX` (SQLSTATE 54001) for a nest of about 80 levels; 70 parse
description: Spark's SQL parser is recursive, so its depth is bounded by the JVM thread's stack. A statement nested past what the stack takes makes `spark.sql` raise a `ParseException` with the condition `FAILED_TO_PARSE_TOO_COMPLEX` (SQLSTATE 54001) and run nothing; the driver also logs the whole statement, 299 KB at the depth below.

The probe (`python -m sverify_dev.spark_parser_depth`) filters 3,000 rows on a guarded column nested to n levels of `(z > 0) | e` and `(z > 0) & e`, the SQL sverify writes for a nest of bound guards (#2030). The statement grows by about 3 KB per level on average: 9.7 KB at 10 levels, 26 KB at 20, 231 KB at 70, 299 KB at 80. At 70 levels every run parsed it; at 80 levels two runs on a fresh JVM were refused and a run that had parsed the smaller levels first accepted it, so the depth is not a fixed number: it moves with how the JVM has compiled the parser (compiled frames are smaller than interpreted ones). The fact claims no threshold, and a plan near 80 levels may or may not parse.

Time is in the optimizer, not the parser: at 10 levels parse and analysis took 0.6 s and the optimizer 0.3 s; at 20 levels 0.2 s and 0.6 s, under 1 s each; at 70 levels parse and analysis 0.6 to 1.7 s and the optimizer 5 to 15 s of the 6 to 17 s the statement took, with execution under 0.5 s. A run that seemed to hang at 80 levels was the probe's own child process, whose undrained stderr pipe filled while Spark logged the statement; read to the end, the child exits in 12 s.
reference: The reference has no limit on nesting.

evidence.note: rows for 10, 20, 70 and 80 levels with the SQL's size and each phase's time, and the cold-JVM runs at 70 and 80

notes: Spark 4.3.0 (PySpark 4.3.0), local[2], one process per row of `cold`; the refusal is `ParseException` with `getCondition()` = FAILED_TO_PARSE_TOO_COMPLEX, which `sverify_spark.engine.parse_sql` raises as `Unsupported` naming this fact (E1, E2).
